cards.title: Monthly SEO Keyword Evaluation Cycle
cards.summary: Run a recurring monthly review of your target keywords to confirm they are still worth ranking for, and swap them out when they are not.
cards.use_when: Planning the SEO work cadence for your store, or setting up a standing process to decide which categories, collections or blog topics to optimize next.
steps: Pick one focus keyword per cycle rather than trying to optimize everything at once.
At the end of the cycle, check whether that keyword is one you actually want to rank for — i.e. it matches the products you sell and the intent of buyers you want.
If it is not a good fit, choose a different keyword rather than forcing content for it.

Set the review at a monthly cadence as the baseline; the source notes 12 times a year is a reasonable rhythm if you have limited time. Move to weekly or daily only if you have the capacity for the research, writing and publishing each round.
Treat consistency across cycles as the driver of progress, not one-off bursts.
caveats: Monthly is presented as a convenient default, not a proven optimal frequency; more frequent publication is better if you can sustain it.
Keyword choice should be validated against business fit, not just volume.

cards.title: Blog Posts as a Store SEO Engine
cards.summary: Publishing blog content is the practical recurring SEO action recommended for store owners, feeding keyword coverage beyond product and collection pages.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to invest SEO effort for an ecommerce store beyond optimizing product pages and collections.
steps: Commit to writing and publishing blog posts on a recurring schedule as part of the SEO plan.
Pair the publishing cadence with the keyword evaluation cycle so each post targets a keyword you have reviewed and chosen.
Use the blog to cover topics around your products rather than duplicating product page copy.
Keep going consistently — the source compares SEO to making fine wine over time, not something that improves the day after you start.
If time allows, increase frequency (weekly, or even daily) rather than staying at the monthly baseline.
caveats: The fine-wine framing is an analogy for patience, not measured evidence of a specific ranking timeline.
Results are not promised; content is one input among many.

cards.title: Optimize the Homepage as a Foundational SEO Asset
cards.summary: Homepage optimization is one of the concrete first implementation actions a store owner should take after learning SEO fundamentals.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing which pages to optimize first on a store — particularly when the store's homepage is thin, unclear or not aligned to target keywords.
steps: Treat the homepage as a page worth explicit SEO work, not just a visual storefront.
Align the homepage's on-page content with the keywords you have researched and decided to target.
Pair homepage optimization with keyword research so the page targets terms that match what you sell.
Run homepage optimization alongside building out blog content rather than instead of it.
Re-check homepage keyword fit during the recurring keyword evaluation cycle.
caveats: The source lists homepage optimization and keyword research as participant-stated implementation actions, not as a ranked priority list.
Keyword research should precede or accompany page optimization so you are not guessing at target terms.

cards.title: Anchor SEO Work With Analytics and Search Console
cards.summary: Google Analytics and Google Search Console are named as the measurement tools that should accompany store SEO implementation.
cards.use_when: Setting up measurement before or alongside SEO changes on a store so you can verify indexing, query performance and traffic.
steps: Connect Google Analytics and Google Search Console as part of your store's SEO setup.
Use Search Console to check how your pages and target keywords are performing in search.
Use Analytics to see what traffic and behavior the SEO work is producing.
Feed what you learn back into the monthly keyword evaluation — drop keywords that are not working out and choose replacements.
Verify current setup steps in each tool's interface, since these products change over time.
caveats: The source names these tools but does not prescribe specific reports or metrics; verify current interfaces before configuring.
Tool access alone does not improve rankings — it supports the keyword selection and evaluation decisions.

cards.title: Consistency Over Intensity in Store SEO
cards.summary: Repeated, steady SEO execution is presented as the key behavior that compounds, rather than occasional large efforts.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to schedule SEO work on your store when you have limited time and must decide between sporadic big pushes or a steady cadence.
steps: Set a cadence you can actually sustain — the source's baseline example is a monthly cycle of keyword research, content writing and publishing.
Repeat the cycle: research keywords, write the content, publish, then review results next cycle.
Resist switching keywords too early; evaluate them at the end of a cycle before replacing them.
Scale frequency up only if you have spare capacity, rather than committing to a pace you will abandon.
Expect compounding, not immediate results — the source explicitly frames SEO growth like aging fine wine.
caveats: 'Consistency is key' is the presenter's opinion, supported by analogy rather than measured data.
The fine-wine comparison does not establish a numeric timeframe for results.
